correctness.rationale: For distinct vertices, distance is two within one part and one across parts, so the faces are exactly within-part sets and partial transversals. The transversal join is connected for two or more parts; gluing each contractible part simplex along its discrete vertex set adds a-1 circles by homotopy pushout. The join is a wedge of the stated top spheres, or a cone if a part is singleton. For at least three parts its H_1 vanishes; the pair sequence gives the integral sum of the part augmentation lattices in degree one, and ordered join chains give the sign on permuting top tensor factors. For two parts, collapsing both disjoint shore simplices gives a two-vertex multigraph with one oriented edge per cross-pair. The cycle lattice is the coefficient-sum kernel and a shore exchange negates the cross-edge action. The maximal faces are the full transversals and nonsingleton full parts; the stated purity and lower-degree obstruction to shellability follow. The verifier's recorded 112 cases and field-rank/sign checks are corroboration, not a proof of the infinite integral theorem or a fresh replay.
